Not advised during Covid - 19 pandemic!
Mar 2020
Baozi takes the claim of Taiwanese culture but the origin of the word Baozi is from China, that information alone should be enough to tell you how the rest of this review will go...

Decided to take the misses to go to a fancy restaurant and as many of you will conclude, the pictures look nice so it can't be that bad right?!

FOR ROMANCE:
Sigh* like the cheap culture of its origin, single tables are placed into pairs to save on logistics cost, so my alone time with the misses turned into a double date with another person's girlfriend. I COULD HEAR HIS CONVERSATION and he could hear mine. - I asked to be moved to a table behind me which was meant for 4 people where the occupants had just left and offered to pay double to the bill than that of what I would eat. Staff's answer was sorry reserved for a customer arriving in 30 minutes... 1 hour later - STILL EMPTY.

HEALTH RISK: Covid-19 or coronavirus requires limited contact so I don't know why they thought to put tables together was going to help with the current PANDEMIC. In their defense, they offered compulsory hand cleansing before entering! If only someone told China and Taiwan that... Chris Huynh! get a noble prize! who needs a vaccine when you have hand sanitizers!

FOOD:
The menu offers Sichuan dishes which are known for the pepper which gives it a unique taste, so when I asked do any of the dishes and Boaz have Sichuan pepper in it? - NOPE! so basicly it's name is purely FALSE advertising.

Taiwanese pork belly rice: Soggy rice which went horribly with pickled greens which ended up giving me acid reflex, tofu wasn't crispy, Pork and eggs were the only thing eatable which is awesome if Keto was still in trend.

The HONEY CHICKEN: the oil was soaked into the flour which instead of giving it a crisp made it soggy and horrible taste. The honey was sweet because of added sugar or just simply cheap suppliers. The size of the wings and drumstick was another illusion from the flour. Once my misses couldn't eat the outer layer, she removed it to find the meat of the actual food, TINY!

BAOS delivered on the Instagram-worthy presentation which of course if it didn't would ruin the strategy of tricking customers to come in and overpay once... after all, if the 7 million citizens of***tried Baozi once and paid 10 dollars, Chris makes 70 million USD.

Atmosphere was playing Weeknd's album on repeat which I am a fan but turned up so that I would have to raise my voice but because there was another conversation next to me, meant that I would have to wait until I was out of the restaurant in order to express how bad the experience was... PURE GENIUS!

-Yes, the BAOS were crap!
Buns were sweat, dry and unbalanced with lack of passion.
PS: why is a Taiwanese/Chinese restaurant selling katsu, tempura, and kimchi(Japanese/Korean) food??? I guess that's what happens when you get a Vietnamese Londoner who opens up a Taiwan restaurant.....

If you are still going to try Baozi after reading this post, then try the Baozi milk tea served in a stainless steel mug(cheap). Or you know... learn photoshop and crop yourself to get the picture.

Horrible service, low standards, unskilled chefs, not ready for international customers.
Dec 2019
I went there many times in the past, but never again. I asked the waiter to give me the eggs benedict with the eggs well done (because they were undercooked, still raw last time). The waiter returned to my table and said the cook refused to cook my eggs well done. I asked why, the waiter said because the cook said so. I then asked to speak with the manager, thinking the manager would ask the chef to do his job, but also the manager said the cook won't do it. I said the cook used to make them for me well done all the time, but the manager insisted on following the cooks orders. So, I left and went to the French restaurant where they have proper chefs who have the skills to leave a poached egg in the water and extra 15 seconds. Very low standards, not ready for international customers. I won't ever go back and will recommend others stay away and spend their money elsewhere for a higher standard of service. It used to be a good restaurant, but not anymore it seems.

Great food and atmosphere.
Dec 2019 • Family
Great food and atmosphere. Craft beers available. Cocktails were well made. We ordered too much food and therefore found the price a little high. The portions are large. I’d suggest you order only one or two dishes at a time, regardless of whether they are shown as starters or mains on the menu. We saw quite a few people taking the food they could not finish away. 

I’d describe the food as Asian fusion. It’s delicious, but not traditional Vietnamese nor Bao. 

Be aware that you may have to pay a 10% service fee. 

We asked local Vietnamese customers about the service fee and they said they also paid the service fee.
